This is useful for lightweight, stateless services where you want to ensure that each consumer gets a fresh instance. Scoped services, on the other hand, are created once per request within the scope of a single HTTP request. This means that if you inject a scoped service into multiple components during the same request, they will all receive the same instance, which is beneficial for services that need to maintain state throughout a single request but not beyond it. Lastly, singleton services are created once and shared throughout the application's lifetime. This means that all requests and components that require a singleton service will receive the same instance, which can be advantageous for services that are expensive to create or that maintain shared state.
